title: Top 5 KPI dashboard software for agencies and service businesses in 2026
summary: Still building your margin spreadsheet by hand each month? Compare 5 KPI dashboard tools for agencies in 2026 and see how one digital agency built its own.
body_markdown:
It’s the fourth working day of the month. Your operations lead has timesheets exported from one tool, invoices from your accounting software, and a project budget sheet nobody has touched in three weeks. She’s pasting all of it into a spreadsheet to answer one question: did the Henderson rollout make money in October? By the time the number is right, the team has logged another 40 hours against a budget that ran out last week.


I have spent the last several years watching service businesses try to get a clear picture of how they are performing. The pattern is almost always the same. The dashboard tool is rarely the problem. The problem is that the numbers it needs (hours logged, budgets, invoices) live in four places and only meet once a month, in someone’s spreadsheet.


This guide compares five KPI dashboard tools for agencies, consultancies, and other[professional services firms](https://noloco.io/solutions/professional-services) , with a focus on the two things owners ask about most: how each project is doing against its budget, and how much revenue is coming in.


## Which dashboard software should agencies use for real-time project and revenue KPIs?


It depends on where your project numbers live today. If your hours, budgets, and invoices already sit in clean, connected systems, a dashboard tool like Looker Studio or Databox is enough. If they don’t, you need a tool that holds the data and does the math, not just one that draws the chart.


In practice, agencies and professional services firms end up choosing between three types of tool:


- **Dashboard and reporting tools** (Looker Studio, Databox, Klipfolio): pull numbers from your other tools and show them on one screen. Best when your data is already clean.
- **PSA tools** (Productive, Scoro, Teamwork): run time tracking, budgets, and invoicing in one place, so margin and budget burn come built in. Best when your delivery process matches how the tool works.
- **Portal builders** (Noloco): build the project tracker, the dashboard, and the client portal around the way your business already works, on your existing data. Best when your projects have steps, exceptions, or client involvement that a standard template doesn’t cover.


## What should you look for before you pick a tool?


Most dashboard software was built for SaaS, ecommerce, or finance teams. Service firms sell hours and expertise, so the numbers that matter are different. Before you compare features, answer these five questions:


- **Do clients need to see it, or is it internal only?** A partner checking firm-wide margin and a client checking how much of their retainer is left need very different access rules.
- **Where does your data live?** List every place hours, budgets, and invoices are recorded today. If a tool can’t connect to all of them, someone will keep exporting files by hand.
- **Does the tool calculate your KPIs, or only display them?** A chart of project margin is only useful if something upstream works out cost (hours times each person’s cost rate) and compares it to what you billed.
- **Do you need project-level KPIs, firm-level KPIs, or both?** “Is the Henderson project over budget?” and “Is utilization dropping across the firm?” need different data underneath.
- **How much setup time do you have?** Some tools take an afternoon. Others need weeks of configuration and someone who enjoys formulas.


One note on search results: if you search for “agency dashboard software”, many results are marketing reporting tools such as AgencyAnalytics or DashThis. Those are built to show clients their ad and campaign results. They’re good at that, but they won’t tell you whether your own projects are making money.


## Which project and revenue KPIs should an agency dashboard show?


Start with the numbers that change what you do this week, not the ones that look good in a board pack. For most agencies and consultancies, that’s a short list: how busy people are, whether each project is on budget, and whether the work done is turning into invoices.


Utilization deserves a close eye right now. Billable utilization across professional services fell to 66.4% in 2025, the lowest in the survey’s history, according to the[SPI Research 2026 Professional Services Maturity Benchmark](https://www.certinia.com/blog/analyzing-the-2026-spi-research-professional-services-maturity-benchmark-report/) (509 firms surveyed). And getting these numbers is still slow work: 72% of project professionals spend half a day or more each month pulling reports together ([Wellingtone, State of Project Management 2026](https://pmworldlibrary.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/260316-Wellingtone-state-of-PM-2026-press-release.pdf) ).


The table below lists the KPIs that matter most, what each one answers, and the data you need for it. For definitions, see our guides to[agency KPIs](https://noloco.io/glossary/agency-kpis) and[project margin](https://noloco.io/glossary/project-margin) .


KPI What it answers Data you need


**Billable utilization** How much of each person’s paid time goes into client work? Hours logged per person, marked billable or not, and their available hours


**Budget burn** How much of this project’s budget is used, and will it run out before the work is done? Project budget in hours or money, hours logged against the project


**[Project margin](https://noloco.io/glossary/project-margin)** After paying for the time, did this project make money? Revenue billed for the project, hours logged, each person’s cost rate


**Unbilled work** How much finished work hasn’t been invoiced yet? Billable hours logged, invoices already sent


**Time to invoice** How long between finishing the work and sending the bill? Work completion dates, invoice dates


**Retainer hours used** How many of this month’s retainer hours has the client used? Hours included per retainer, hours logged per client


**On-time delivery** What share of projects and milestones finish by the agreed date? Due dates and actual completion dates per milestone


Notice the “data you need” column. Every one of these KPIs depends on hours being logged against the right project and the right person’s cost rate. If that part is messy, no dashboard tool will fix it.

## 1. What is Noloco best for?


Noloco is an AI portal builder for businesses whose operations don’t fit a template. Instead of adding a dashboard on top of other tools, you build the project tracker, the KPI dashboard, and the client portal in one place, on the data you already have. Full disclosure: I built it, so weigh this section accordingly.


**Where it works for project and revenue KPIs:** describe what you need to[Nola, Noloco’s AI builder](https://noloco.io/product/nola) (for example, “a dashboard showing budget burn per project and unbilled hours per client”) and it builds the pages for you.[Noloco charts](https://noloco.io/product/charts) update with your live data and can be filtered by client, owner, status, or due date. Because the data and the dashboard live in the same system, a partner sees firm-wide margin, a project lead sees their own projects, and a client sees only their own retainer balance, each based on[role-based permissions](https://noloco.io/product/permissions) .


You can keep your data where it is. Noloco connects to[Airtable](https://noloco.io/data/airtable) , Google Sheets, HubSpot, Postgres, and other sources, or you can use Noloco’s own tables.[Workflows](https://noloco.io/product/workflows) handle the follow-up, such as notifying a project lead when logged hours pass 80% of the budget.


GAP Consulting is a real example. After moving billing into Noloco, they switched to automated bi-weekly invoicing, doubled their cash flow, and increased billable hours by 50%. Read the[GAP Consulting customer story](https://noloco.io/customer-stories/gap-consulting) .


It Just So Happens, a fully remote digital agency, runs its projects, risks, and escalations through a portal built on Noloco. As founder Taelon Vorster puts it: “It’s the first time since starting the business that I have entire visibility whilst being invisible.” Read the[It Just So Happens customer story](https://noloco.io/customer-stories/it-just-so-happens-digital-agency) .


**Where it falls short:** Noloco doesn’t come with a fixed margin formula. You decide how cost and margin are worked out, which is the point for firms with unusual billing, but it’s a step PSA tools skip. Klipfolio (below) offers more chart types, and PSA tools go deeper on capacity planning across large teams.


**Best for:** agencies and consultancies whose projects have steps, approvals, or client involvement that standard tools don’t handle, and that want clients in the same system as the team.


**Pricing:** the Free plan includes unlimited team seats and 50 active clients. The Build plan includes 10 team seats (then $5 for each extra activated seat) and 1,000 active clients. A firm with 15 staff and 400 client and subcontractor logins fits on one Build plan. See[Noloco pricing](https://noloco.io/pricing) .


## 2. What is Looker Studio best for?


Looker Studio is Google’s free reporting tool. It connects to Google Sheets, BigQuery, Google Analytics, and a long list of partner connectors, and turns them into shareable reports.


**Where it works for project and revenue KPIs:** if your timesheets and budgets already sit in a well-kept Google Sheet, Looker Studio can show budget burn by project and revenue by month for free. Reports refresh when the underlying sheet changes.


**Where it falls short:** it doesn’t store data or calculate anything you haven’t already set up in the source. Keeping that sheet accurate is the real work, and it usually lands on one person. Sharing works through Google accounts or links; showing each client only their own rows needs extra setup in the data source.


**Best for:** firms with clean data in Google Sheets or BigQuery and someone comfortable maintaining it.


**Pricing:** free, with a paid Pro version for teams. See[Looker Studio](https://lookerstudio.google.com/) .


## 3. What is Databox best for?


Databox pulls metrics from many tools (CRMs, accounting software, analytics) into one screen, with goals and scorecards on top. It’s quick to set up if your tools are on its list of integrations.


**Where it works for project and revenue KPIs:** top-line revenue, pipeline value, and invoiced amounts from your CRM and accounting tool, side by side and updated on a schedule.


**Where it falls short:** Databox shows what your other tools already report. If none of them works out project margin or budget vs actual, Databox can’t either. Client sharing exists, but it’s built for showing clients marketing and sales results, not for clients approving work or checking project status.


**Best for:** leadership teams that want revenue and pipeline numbers in one place, with delivery tracked elsewhere.


**Pricing:** free tier and paid plans. See[Databox pricing](https://databox.com/pricing) .


## 4. What is Klipfolio best for?


Klipfolio is one of the most flexible tools on this list. It has a strong connector library, a formula engine, and two products: Klips for custom dashboards and PowerMetrics for defining metrics once and reusing them.


**Where it works for project and revenue KPIs:** if you can pull time, budget, and invoice data into it, you can build almost any calculation, including margin by project or utilization by team.


**Where it falls short:** that flexibility takes time. Expect a real setup project, and someone who keeps the formulas working as your tools change. It’s built for internal reporting rather than client access.


**Best for:** firms with an analyst or a data-minded operations lead who wants full control over every metric.


**Pricing:** see[Klipfolio pricing](https://www.klipfolio.com/pricing) .


## 5. What is monday.com best for?


monday.com is a project management tool first, with dashboards built on top of its boards. If your projects already run there, adding a dashboard takes minutes.


**Where it works for project and revenue KPIs:** project status, workload by person, deadlines at risk, and hours logged through its time tracking column, all in one view.


**Where it falls short:** dashboards are secondary to project management. Project margin needs formula columns or a separate setup, and firm-wide financial reporting is limited. Clients can join as guests, which are unlimited on Pro and Enterprise plans (on Standard, every 4 guests count as 1 paid seat), but guests only see the boards shared with them, so margin data has to live on separate boards ([monday.com guest access](https://support.monday.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005340405) ).


**Best for:** teams already running projects in monday.com that mainly need status and workload views.


**Pricing:** see[monday.com pricing](https://monday.com/pricing) .


## What about PSA tools like Productive, Scoro, and Teamwork?


PSA (professional services automation) tools aren’t dashboard tools, but they belong in this conversation. They run time tracking, budgets, and invoicing in one system, so project and revenue KPIs come built in instead of being stitched together. See our[guide to PSA software](https://noloco.io/glossary/psa-software) for the full picture.


- **Productive** tracks profitability in real time as hours are logged, forecasts budget overruns, and sends alerts before a project runs out of money. Clients can be added free of charge, with permissions over what they see, including budgets ([Productive client portal](https://productive.io/client-portal/) ).
- **Scoro** covers the path from quote to invoice, with quoted vs actual reports, work-in-progress reports, and revenue forecasts on its higher plans. Reviewers often mention a steep learning curve at the start.
- **Teamwork** has a profitability report that shows revenue, cost, profit, and margin by project and person, available on its Optimize and Enterprise plans ([Teamwork help center](https://support.teamwork.com/projects/reports/profitability-report) ).


The trade-off is fit. PSA tools work best when your delivery follows the process they were designed around: log time, track against budget, invoice. If your projects involve field visits, multi-stage approvals, subcontractors, or clients submitting information mid-project, you’ll either bend your process to the tool or track those parts somewhere else. That’s usually the moment firms look at building their own system instead.


## Final thoughts


The right KPI dashboard is the one your team keeps up to date without being chased. For most agencies and consultancies, that means solving where the numbers live first and choosing the chart tool second.


If your data is already clean and connected, Looker Studio or Databox will get you a good view for little money. If you want margin and budget burn without building anything, and your process matches theirs, a PSA tool like Productive is worth a trial. If your operation has steps, exceptions, or client involvement that standard tools don’t cover, building your own tracker and dashboard on Noloco keeps the team, the numbers, and your clients in one place.
